Index: .opencode/plugins/entire.ts
===================================================================
--- .opencode/plugins/entire.ts	
+++ .opencode/plugins/entire.ts	
@@ -0,0 +1,177 @@
+// Entire CLI plugin for OpenCode
+// Auto-generated by `entire enable --agent opencode`
+// Do not edit manually — changes will be overwritten on next install.
+// Requires Bun runtime (used by OpenCode's plugin system for loading ESM plugins).
+import type { Plugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"
+
+export const EntirePlugin: Plugin = async ({ directory }) => {
+  const ENTIRE_CMD = 'entire'
+  // Track seen user messages to fire turn-start only once per message
+  const seenUserMessages = new Set<string>()
+  // Track current session ID for message events (which don't include sessionID)
+  let currentSessionID: string | null = null
+  // Track the model used by the most recent assistant message
+  let currentModel: string | null = null
+  // In-memory store for message metadata (role, tokens, etc.)
+  const messageStore = new Map<string, any>()
+
+  /**
+   * Build the shell command for a hook invocation.
+   * Uses sh -c so that shell command substitution in ENTIRE_CMD
+   * (e.g., $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) for local-dev) is interpreted.
+   */
+  function hookCmd(hookName: string): string[] {
+    return ["sh", "-c", `${ENTIRE_CMD} hooks opencode ${hookName}`]
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Pipe JSON payload to an entire hooks command (async).
+   * Errors are logged but never thrown — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode.
+   */
+  async function callHook(hookName: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>) {
+    try {
+      const json = JSON.stringify(payload)
+      const proc = Bun.spawn(hookCmd(hookName), {
+        cwd: directory,
+        stdin: new Blob([json + "\n"]),
+        stdout: "ignore",
+        stderr: "ignore",
+      })
+      await proc.exited
+    } catch {
+      // Silently ignore — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode
+    }
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Synchronous variant for hooks that fire near process exit (turn-end, session-end).
+   * `opencode run` breaks its event loop on the same session.status idle event that
+   * triggers turn-end. The async callHook would be killed before completing.
+   * Bun.spawnSync blocks the event loop, preventing exit until the hook finishes.
+   */
+  function callHookSync(hookName: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>) {
+    try {
+      const json = JSON.stringify(payload)
+      Bun.spawnSync(hookCmd(hookName), {
+        cwd: directory,
+        stdin: new TextEncoder().encode(json + "\n"),
+        stdout: "ignore",
+        stderr: "ignore",
+      })
+    } catch {
+      // Silently ignore — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode
+    }
+  }
+
+  return {
+    event: async ({ event }) => {
+      try {
+        switch (event.type) {
+          case "session.created": {
+            const session = (event as any).properties?.info
+            if (!session?.id) break
+            // Reset per-session tracking state when switching sessions.
+            if (currentSessionID !== session.id) {
+              seenUserMessages.clear()
+              messageStore.clear()
+              currentModel = null
+              await callHook("session-start", {
+                session_id: session.id,
+              })
+            }
+            currentSessionID = session.id
+            break
+          }
+
+          case "message.updated": {
+            const msg = (event as any).properties?.info
+            if (!msg) break
+            // Store message metadata (role, time, tokens, etc.)
+            messageStore.set(msg.id, msg)
+            // Track model from assistant messages
+            if (msg.role === "assistant" && msg.modelID) {
+              currentModel = msg.modelID
+            }
+            break
+          }
+
+          case "message.part.updated": {
+            const part = (event as any).properties?.part
+            if (!part?.messageID) break
+
+            // Fire turn-start on the first text part of a new user message
+            const msg = messageStore.get(part.messageID)
+            if (msg?.role === "user" && part.type === "text" && !seenUserMessages.has(msg.id)) {
+              seenUserMessages.add(msg.id)
+              const sessionID = msg.sessionID ?? currentSessionID
+              if (sessionID) {
+                await callHook("turn-start", {
+                  session_id: sessionID,
+                  prompt: part.text ?? "",
+                  model: currentModel ?? "",
+                })
+              }
+            }
+            break
+          }
+
+          case "session.status": {
+            // session.status fires in both TUI and non-interactive (run) mode.
+            // session.idle is deprecated and not reliably emitted in run mode.
+            const props = (event as any).properties
+            if (props?.status?.type !== "idle") break
+            const sessionID = props?.sessionID ?? currentSessionID
+            if (!sessionID) break
+            // Use sync variant: `opencode run` exits on the same idle event,
+            // so an async hook would be killed before completing.
+            callHookSync("turn-end", {
+              session_id: sessionID,
+              model: currentModel ?? "",
+            })
+            break
+          }
+
+          case "session.compacted": {
+            const sessionID = (event as any).properties?.sessionID
+            if (!sessionID) break
+            await callHook("compaction", {
+              session_id: sessionID,
+            })
+            break
+          }
+
+          case "session.deleted": {
+            const session = (event as any).properties?.info
+            if (!session?.id) break
+            seenUserMessages.clear()
+            messageStore.clear()
+            currentSessionID = null
+            // Use sync variant: session-end may fire during shutdown.
+            callHookSync("session-end", {
+              session_id: session.id,
+            })
+            break
+          }
+
+          case "server.instance.disposed": {
+            // Fires when OpenCode shuts down (TUI close or `opencode run` exit).
+            // session.deleted only fires on explicit user deletion, not on quit,
+            // so this is the only reliable way to end sessions on exit.
+            if (!currentSessionID) break
+            const sessionID = currentSessionID
+            seenUserMessages.clear()
+            messageStore.clear()
+            currentSessionID = null
+            // Use sync variant: this is the last event before process exit.
+            callHookSync("session-end", {
+              session_id: sessionID,
+            })
+            break
+          }
+        }
+      } catch {
+        // Silently ignore — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode
+      }
+    },
+  }
+}

Index: README.md
===================================================================
--- README.md	
+++ README.md	
@@ -0,0 +1,89 @@
+# Reflex — AI Call Tracker
+
+System-wide network interception + cross-session memory layer for AI apps on macOS.
+Intercepts traffic from ChatGPT.app, Claude.app, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI,
+Raycast AI, etc. so agents can share context and mistakes across sessions.
+
+## Architecture
+
+```
+ ┌──────────────────────────┐    WS/JSON    ┌───────────────────────────┐
+ │  Electron app (TS/React) │ ◀───────────▶ │ Rust sidecar (hudsucker) │
+ │  SQLite · flow browser   │               │ MITM · CA · proxy        │
+ └──────────────────────────┘               └───────────────────────────┘
+                                                        │
+                                                        ▼
+                                        macOS hooks (networksetup + pf + shell env)
+```
+
+Two working directories:
+
+- `electron/` — Electron + React + TypeScript shell (UI + storage + orchestration)
+- `rust/`     — Rust capture sidecar (hudsucker MITM, rustls, WebSocket IPC)
+- `webapp/`   — reserved for future web dashboard (empty placeholder)
+- `scripts/`  — install hooks and sidecar build helpers
+
+## Quick start
+
+```bash
+# 1. Build the Rust sidecar (release, ~8 MB; ~1 min cold)
+./scripts/build-sidecar.sh
+
+# 2. Install deps and run the Electron app in dev
+cd electron
+pnpm install    # postinstall rebuilds better-sqlite3 for Electron's Node ABI
+pnpm dev
+```
+
+The first time the sidecar starts it generates a local CA at
+`~/Library/Application Support/Reflex/capture/reflex-ca.pem`. The Electron
+shell will later prompt (via `sudo-prompt`) to:
+
+- install that CA into the System keychain (so HTTPS MITM is trusted)
+- set the macOS HTTP/HTTPS proxy to `127.0.0.1:8888`
+- (optionally, future work) add pf redirect rules for transparent capture
+
+To instrument CLI tools (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI), enable the
+"Instrument shell" toggle in Settings — it will append `HTTPS_PROXY` and
+`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` to your `~/.zshrc`.
+
+### Manual sanity check (no Electron needed)
+
+```bash
+# Start the sidecar on random ports with capture-everything mode
+REFLEX_DATA_DIR=/tmp/reflex ./rust/target/release/reflex-capture \
+  --proxy-port 0 --ws-port 0
+
+# In another shell, run curl through it (self-signed CA → use -k)
+curl -k -x http://127.0.0.1:<proxy_port> https://example.com/
+# ...watch live events on ws://127.0.0.1:<ws_port>
+```
+
+## MVP milestones
+
+- [x] Electron ↔ Rust sidecar wired over WebSocket
+- [x] Auto-generate CA + stdout `sidecar_ready` handshake
+- [x] End-to-end MITM verified (`curl -k` through proxy → WS events)
+- [x] SQLite store for flows + bodies (better-sqlite3)
+- [x] React list/detail flow viewer
+- [ ] CA + proxy install via `sudo-prompt` on first launch
+- [ ] Shell env injection for CLI tools (HTTPS_PROXY, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS)
+- [ ] Export "mistakes" context file for CLI agents
+
+## Host allowlist (MVP)
+
+`api.openai.com`, `api.anthropic.com`, `chat.openai.com`, `claude.ai`,
+`api.cursor.sh`, `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, `api.x.ai`
+
+## Event schema
+
+The sidecar emits newline-delimited JSON over WebSocket. See
+`rust/src/event.rs` and `electron/src/shared/types.ts` — they must stay in sync.
+
+## Known risks
+
+| Risk | Mitigation |
+|---|---|
+| Cert pinning (ChatGPT.app likely pins) | Fallback to file-watching local session stores |
+| First-run admin prompts | One-time `sudo-prompt` flow with onboarding UX |
+| Network Extension entitlement needed for some apps | Capture layer is behind an interface — backends swappable |

+    <!-- Inbound loopback for the local WebSocket + MITM proxy. -->

+appId: ai.reflex.desktop
+productName: Reflex
+copyright: Copyright © 2026 Reflex
+
+directories:
+  buildResources: build
+  output: dist
+
+files:
+  - "out/**/*"
+  - "package.json"
+
+extraResources:
+  - from: "resources/capture"
+    to: "capture"
+  - from: "../scripts/install-hooks.sh"

+asar: true

+  target:
+    - target: dmg
+      arch:
+        - arm64
+    - target: zip
+      arch:
+        - arm64

+  gatekeeperAssess: false
+  entitlements: build/entitlements.mac.plist
+  entitlementsInherit: build/entitlements.mac.plist

--- rust/Cargo.toml	
+++ rust/Cargo.toml	
@@ -0,0 +1,57 @@
+[package]
+name = "reflex-capture"
+version = "0.1.0"
+edition = "2021"
+rust-version = "1.85"
+description = "Reflex MITM capture sidecar — intercepts AI API traffic and streams events to the Electron shell over WebSocket"
+
+[[bin]]
+name = "reflex-capture"
+path = "src/main.rs"
+
+[dependencies]
+# MITM engine (rcgen-ca + rustls-client are default features)
+hudsucker = { version = "0.24", features = ["decoder", "http2"] }
+
+# Certificate authority
+rcgen = { version = "0.14", features = ["pem"] }
+time = "0.3"
+
+# Async runtime and primitives
+tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }
+tokio-tungstenite = "0.28"
+futures-util = "0.3"
+
+# TLS provider used by hudsucker is re-exported; we just use the aws_lc_rs
+# default provider that matches hudsucker's own examples.
+
+# HTTP utilities
+http = "1"
+http-body-util = "0.1"
+bytes = "1"
+
+# Serialization / IDs / time
+serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
+serde_json = "1"
+uuid = { version = "1", features = ["v4", "serde"] }
+chrono = { version = "0.4", features = ["serde"] }
+base64 = "0.22"
+
+# CLI and logging
+clap = { version = "4", features = ["derive", "env"] }
+tracing = "0.1"
+tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", features = ["env-filter"] }
+
+# Errors + filesystem
+anyhow = "1"
+thiserror = "2"
+dirs = "5"
+
+# Hashing (CA fingerprint)
+sha2 = "0.10"
+

+# reflex-capture (Rust sidecar)
+
+MITM proxy + local WebSocket event stream. Spawned by the Electron shell.
+
+## Run standalone
+
+```bash
+cargo run -- \
+  --proxy-port 8888 \
+  --ws-port 0 \
+  --data-dir ~/.reflex \
+  --allow-host api.anthropic.com \
+  --allow-host api.openai.com
+```
+
+On start it prints one line of JSON on stdout (`sidecar_ready`) with the bound
+proxy port, WS port, CA cert path, and CA fingerprint. After that, events
+stream to every connected WebSocket client as JSON text frames.
+
+## Environment variables
+
+| Var                 | Equivalent flag      |
+|---------------------|----------------------|
+| `REFLEX_PROXY_PORT` | `--proxy-port`       |
+| `REFLEX_WS_PORT`    | `--ws-port`          |
+| `REFLEX_DATA_DIR`   | `--data-dir`         |
+| `REFLEX_ALLOW_HOSTS`| `--allow-host` (csv) |
+| `REFLEX_LOG`        | tracing `EnvFilter`  |
+
+## Wire events
+
+See `src/event.rs` — tagged union. The TypeScript mirror is in
+`electron/src/shared/types.ts` and must stay in sync.
+
+## Caveats
+
+- Bodies are buffered up to 10 MiB in memory per side; larger responses
+  are truncated (the `truncated` flag goes `true`). Streaming / chunked
+  event relay is future work.
+- WebSocket upgrades through the proxy are not yet instrumented (there's a
+  `WebSocketHandler` hook in hudsucker we don't use yet).
+- `handle_error` vs. `FlowEnd` races are best-effort — on a very fast
+  error path we may miss the tail event.

+//! Wire event schema shared with the Electron shell.
+//!
+//! Every event is a JSON object tagged by `type`. The Electron side's
+//! `electron/src/shared/types.ts` must stay in sync with this module.
+
+use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
+use std::collections::BTreeMap;
+
+pub type Headers = BTreeMap<String, String>;
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")]
+pub enum CaptureEvent {
+    /// Emitted once on startup so the shell knows where to find the CA.
+    SidecarReady {
+        proxy_port: u16,
+        ws_port: u16,
+        ca_cert_path: String,
+        ca_fingerprint_sha256: String,
+    },
+
+    /// A new flow has begun. A flow id ties requests and responses together.
+    FlowStart {
+        id: String,
+        ts: String,
+        method: String,
+        scheme: String,
+        host: String,
+        port: u16,
+        path: String,
+        url: String,
+        http_version: String,
+    },
+
+    /// Request headers (sent immediately after FlowStart).
+    RequestHead { id: String, headers: Headers },
+
+    /// Request body bytes (base64). May be chunked in the future; MVP sends one chunk.
+    RequestBody {
+        id: String,
+        body_b64: String,
+        truncated: bool,
+        byte_len: usize,
+    },
+
+    /// Response status line + headers.
+    ResponseHead {
+        id: String,
+        status: u16,
+        http_version: String,
+        headers: Headers,
+    },
+
+    /// Response body bytes (base64, decoded if compressed).
+    ResponseBody {
+        id: String,
+        body_b64: String,
+        truncated: bool,
+        byte_len: usize,
+    },
+
+    /// Flow finished (success or error).
+    FlowEnd {
+        id: String,
+        duration_ms: u64,
+        error: Option<String>,
+    },
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Build the Rust capture sidecar and copy the binary into
+# electron/resources/ so the Electron main process can spawn it.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   scripts/build-sidecar.sh [--release]
+#
+# Defaults to a release build. Pass --debug for a faster incremental dev build.
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+profile="release"
+for arg in "$@"; do
+  case "$arg" in
+    --release) profile="release" ;;
+    --debug)   profile="dev" ;;
+    -h|--help)
+      echo "Usage: $0 [--release|--debug]"
+      exit 0
+      ;;
+    *)
+      echo "unknown arg: $arg" >&2
+      exit 2
+      ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+root_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+rust_dir="$root_dir/rust"
+out_dir="$root_dir/electron/resources"
+mkdir -p "$out_dir"
+
+cargo_profile_flag=""
+cargo_subdir="debug"
+if [ "$profile" = "release" ]; then
+  cargo_profile_flag="--release"
+  cargo_subdir="release"
+fi
+
+echo "==> cargo build $cargo_profile_flag  (cwd: $rust_dir)"
+(cd "$rust_dir" && cargo build $cargo_profile_flag)
+
+src_bin="$rust_dir/target/$cargo_subdir/reflex-capture"
+dest_bin="$out_dir/capture"
+
+if [ ! -f "$src_bin" ]; then
+  echo "error: expected binary at $src_bin" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+cp "$src_bin" "$dest_bin"
+chmod +x "$dest_bin"
+echo "==> copied $src_bin → $dest_bin"
+ls -lh "$dest_bin"

--- scripts/install-hooks.sh

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Install Reflex capture hooks on macOS:
+#   1. Add the Reflex local CA to the System keychain (trustRoot)
+#   2. Set the HTTP/HTTPS proxy on the primary network service
+#
+# Intended to be run via sudo-prompt from the Electron shell on first launch.
+# Can also be run manually:
+#
+#   scripts/install-hooks.sh --ca /path/to/reflex-ca.pem --proxy-host 127.0.0.1 --proxy-port 8888
+#
+# Use --uninstall to reverse the proxy configuration and remove the CA.
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+CA_PATH=""
+PROXY_HOST="127.0.0.1"
+PROXY_PORT="8888"
+UNINSTALL=0
+
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --ca)         CA_PATH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --proxy-host) PROXY_HOST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --proxy-port) PROXY_PORT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --uninstall)  UNINSTALL=1; shift ;;
+    -h|--help)
+      cat <<EOF
+Usage: $0 [options]
+  --ca <path>          Reflex CA PEM (required unless --uninstall)
+  --proxy-host <host>  default 127.0.0.1
+  --proxy-port <port>  default 8888
+  --uninstall          remove CA + disable proxy
+EOF
+      exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "unknown arg: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+if [ "$(uname -s)" != "Darwin" ]; then
+  echo "This script only supports macOS." >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+if [ "$EUID" -ne 0 ]; then
+  echo "This script must be run as root (it modifies the System keychain and network prefs)." >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+primary_service() {
+  # Pick the first interface whose Device matches the active network route.
+  local dev
+  dev="$(route -n get default 2>/dev/null | awk '/interface:/{print $2}')"
+  if [ -z "$dev" ]; then
+    echo "Wi-Fi"
+    return
+  fi
+  networksetup -listnetworkserviceorder \
+    | awk -v d="$dev" 'match($0, /\(Hardware Port: ([^,]+), Device: ([^)]+)\)/, m) { if (m[2] == d) print m[1] }' \
+    | head -n1
+}
+
+SERVICE="$(primary_service)"
+if [ -z "$SERVICE" ]; then
+  echo "could not determine primary network service; defaulting to Wi-Fi" >&2
+  SERVICE="Wi-Fi"
+fi
+echo "==> primary network service: $SERVICE"
+
+install_ca() {
+  [ -n "$CA_PATH" ] || { echo "missing --ca"; exit 2; }
+  [ -f "$CA_PATH" ] || { echo "CA file not found: $CA_PATH"; exit 2; }
+  echo "==> trusting CA: $CA_PATH"
+  security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot \
+    -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain \
+    "$CA_PATH"
+}
+
+uninstall_ca() {
+  echo "==> removing Reflex CA from System keychain"
+  # Best-effort: remove by CN. We set CN = "Reflex Local MITM CA" in rust/src/ca.rs.
+  security delete-certificate -c "Reflex Local MITM CA" \
+    /Library/Keychains/System.keychain 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+enable_proxy() {
+  echo "==> setting proxy on '$SERVICE' → $PROXY_HOST:$PROXY_PORT"
+  networksetup -setwebproxy       "$SERVICE" "$PROXY_HOST" "$PROXY_PORT"
+  networksetup -setsecurewebproxy "$SERVICE" "$PROXY_HOST" "$PROXY_PORT"
+  networksetup -setwebproxystate       "$SERVICE" on
+  networksetup -setsecurewebproxystate "$SERVICE" on
+}
+
+disable_proxy() {
+  echo "==> disabling proxy on '$SERVICE'"
+  networksetup -setwebproxystate       "$SERVICE" off || true
+  networksetup -setsecurewebproxystate "$SERVICE" off || true
+}
+
+if [ "$UNINSTALL" -eq 1 ]; then
+  disable_proxy
+  uninstall_ca
+  echo "done: Reflex hooks removed."
+else
+  install_ca
+  enable_proxy
+  echo "done: Reflex hooks installed."
+fi

# Reflex — AI Call Tracker

System-wide network interception + cross-session memory layer for AI apps on macOS.
Intercepts traffic from ChatGPT.app, Claude.app, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI,
Raycast AI, etc. so agents can share context and mistakes across sessions.

## Architecture

```
 ┌──────────────────────────┐    WS/JSON    ┌───────────────────────────┐
 │  Electron app (TS/React) │ ◀───────────▶ │ Rust sidecar (hudsucker) │
 │  SQLite · flow browser   │               │ MITM · CA · proxy        │
 └──────────────────────────┘               └───────────────────────────┘
                                                        │
                                                        ▼
                                        macOS hooks (networksetup + pf + shell env)
```

Two working directories:

- `electron/` — Electron + React + TypeScript shell (UI + storage + orchestration)
- `rust/`     — Rust capture sidecar (hudsucker MITM, rustls, WebSocket IPC)
- `webapp/`   — reserved for future web dashboard (empty placeholder)
- `scripts/`  — install hooks and sidecar build helpers

## Quick start

```bash
# 1. Build the Rust sidecar
./scripts/build-sidecar.sh

# 2. Install deps and run the Electron app in dev
cd electron
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

On first launch the app will prompt for admin rights to:

- install a local CA into the System keychain
- set the macOS HTTP/HTTPS proxy to `127.0.0.1:8888`
- (optionally) add pf redirect rules for transparent capture

To instrument CLI tools (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI), enable the
"Instrument shell" toggle in Settings — it appends `HTTPS_PROXY` and
`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` to your `~/.zshrc`.

## MVP milestones

- [ ] Electron ↔ Rust sidecar wired over WebSocket
- [ ] Auto-generate + install CA, set system proxy
- [ ] End-to-end capture of `api.anthropic.com`
- [ ] SQLite store for flows + bodies
- [ ] React list/detail flow viewer
- [ ] Export "mistakes" context file for CLI agents

## Host allowlist (MVP)

`api.openai.com`, `api.anthropic.com`, `chat.openai.com`, `claude.ai`,
`api.cursor.sh`, `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, `api.x.ai`

## Event schema

The sidecar emits newline-delimited JSON over WebSocket. See
`rust/src/event.rs` and `electron/src/shared/types.ts` — they must stay in sync.

## Known risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Cert pinning (ChatGPT.app likely pins) | Fallback to file-watching local session stores |
| First-run admin prompts | One-time `sudo-prompt` flow with onboarding UX |
| Network Extension entitlement needed for some apps | Capture layer is behind an interface — backends swappable |

Expand description

Hudsucker is a MITM HTTP/S proxy that allows you to:

-   Modify HTTP/S requests
-   Modify HTTP/S responses
-   Modify WebSocket messages

### [§](#features)Features

-   `decoder`: Enables [`decode_request`](fn.decode_request.html "fn hudsucker::decode_request") and [`decode_response`](fn.decode_response.html "fn hudsucker::decode_response") helpers (enabled by default).
-   `full`: Enables all features.
-   `http2`: Enables HTTP/2 support.
-   `native-tls-client`: Enables [`ProxyBuilder::with_native_tls_connector`](builder/struct.ProxyBuilder.html#method.with_native_tls_connector "method hudsucker::builder::ProxyBuilder::with_native_tls_connector").
-   `openssl-ca`: Enables [`OpensslAuthority`](certificate_authority/struct.OpensslAuthority.html "struct hudsucker::certificate_authority::OpensslAuthority").
-   `rcgen-ca`: Enables [`RcgenAuthority`](certificate_authority/struct.RcgenAuthority.html "struct hudsucker::certificate_authority::RcgenAuthority") (enabled by default).
-   `rustls-client`: Enables [`ProxyBuilder::with_rustls_connector`](builder/struct.ProxyBuilder.html#method.with_rustls_connector "method hudsucker::builder::ProxyBuilder::with_rustls_connector") (enabled by default).

use hudsucker::{certificate_authority::RcgenAuthority, rustls::crypto::aws_lc_rs};
use rcgen::{Issuer, KeyPair};

let key_pair = include_str!("../../examples/ca/hudsucker.key");
let ca_cert = include_str!("../../examples/ca/hudsucker.cer");
let key_pair = KeyPair::from_pem(key_pair).expect("Failed to parse private key");
let issuer =
    Issuer::from_ca_cert_pem(ca_cert, key_pair).expect("Failed to parse CA certificate");

let ca = RcgenAuthority::new(issuer, 1_000, aws_lc_rs::default_provider());
```

I'm checking the function signature for creating a new instance with an issuer, cache size, and crypto provider, and I see the example uses `aws_lc_rs::default_provider()`. Let me verify whether `ring` would work as an alternative since rustls 0.23 supports both crypto providers.

The problem is that hudsucker likely enables `aws_lc_rs` by default, so if I try to force `ring` with `default-features = false`, I'll run into feature unification conflicts. The simpler approach is to just use `aws_lc_rs` like hudsucker's example does and remove my custom rustls dependency from Cargo.toml to let hudsucker manage it instead.
Let me align with hudsucker's example (`aws_lc_rs` provider):

rustls = { version = "0.23", default-features = false, features = ["ring", "std"] }

# reflex-capture (Rust sidecar)

MITM proxy + local WebSocket event stream. Spawned by the Electron shell.

## Run standalone

```bash
cargo run -- \
  --proxy-port 8888 \
  --ws-port 0 \
  --data-dir ~/.reflex \
  --allow-host api.anthropic.com \
  --allow-host api.openai.com
```

On start it prints one line of JSON on stdout (`sidecar_ready`) with the bound
proxy port, WS port, CA cert path, and CA fingerprint. After that, events
stream to every connected WebSocket client as JSON text frames.

## Environment variables

| Var                 | Equivalent flag      |
|---------------------|----------------------|
| `REFLEX_PROXY_PORT` | `--proxy-port`       |
| `REFLEX_WS_PORT`    | `--ws-port`          |
| `REFLEX_DATA_DIR`   | `--data-dir`         |
| `REFLEX_ALLOW_HOSTS`| `--allow-host` (csv) |
| `REFLEX_LOG`        | tracing `EnvFilter`  |

## Wire events

See `src/event.rs` — tagged union. The TypeScript mirror is in
`electron/src/shared/types.ts` and must stay in sync.

## Caveats

- Bodies are buffered up to 10 MiB in memory per side; larger responses
  are truncated (the `truncated` flag goes `true`). Streaming / chunked
  event relay is future work.
- WebSocket upgrades through the proxy are not yet instrumented (there's a
  `WebSocketHandler` hook in hudsucker we don't use yet).
- `handle_error` vs. `FlowEnd` races are best-effort — on a very fast
  error path we may miss the tail event.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the Rust capture sidecar and copy the binary into
# electron/resources/ so the Electron main process can spawn it.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/build-sidecar.sh [--release]
#
# Defaults to a release build. Pass --debug for a faster incremental dev build.

set -euo pipefail

profile="release"
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --release) profile="release" ;;
    --debug)   profile="dev" ;;
    -h|--help)
      echo "Usage: $0 [--release|--debug]"
      exit 0
      ;;
    *)
      echo "unknown arg: $arg" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done

root_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
rust_dir="$root_dir/rust"
out_dir="$root_dir/electron/resources"
mkdir -p "$out_dir"

cargo_profile_flag=""
cargo_subdir="debug"
if [ "$profile" = "release" ]; then
  cargo_profile_flag="--release"
  cargo_subdir="release"
fi

echo "==> cargo build $cargo_profile_flag  (cwd: $rust_dir)"
(cd "$rust_dir" && cargo build $cargo_profile_flag)

src_bin="$rust_dir/target/$cargo_subdir/reflex-capture"
dest_bin="$out_dir/capture"

if [ ! -f "$src_bin" ]; then
  echo "error: expected binary at $src_bin" >&2
  exit 1
fi

cp "$src_bin" "$dest_bin"
chmod +x "$dest_bin"
echo "==> copied $src_bin → $dest_bin"
ls -lh "$dest_bin"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install Reflex capture hooks on macOS:
#   1. Add the Reflex local CA to the System keychain (trustRoot)
#   2. Set the HTTP/HTTPS proxy on the primary network service
#
# Intended to be run via sudo-prompt from the Electron shell on first launch.
# Can also be run manually:
#
#   scripts/install-hooks.sh --ca /path/to/reflex-ca.pem --proxy-host 127.0.0.1 --proxy-port 8888
#
# Use --uninstall to reverse the proxy configuration and remove the CA.

set -euo pipefail

CA_PATH=""
PROXY_HOST="127.0.0.1"
PROXY_PORT="8888"
UNINSTALL=0

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --ca)         CA_PATH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --proxy-host) PROXY_HOST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --proxy-port) PROXY_PORT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --uninstall)  UNINSTALL=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help)
      cat <<EOF
Usage: $0 [options]
  --ca <path>          Reflex CA PEM (required unless --uninstall)
  --proxy-host <host>  default 127.0.0.1
  --proxy-port <port>  default 8888
  --uninstall          remove CA + disable proxy
EOF
      exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown arg: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

if [ "$(uname -s)" != "Darwin" ]; then
  echo "This script only supports macOS." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$EUID" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "This script must be run as root (it modifies the System keychain and network prefs)." >&2
  exit 1
fi

primary_service() {
  # Pick the first interface whose Device matches the active network route.
  local dev
  dev="$(route -n get default 2>/dev/null | awk '/interface:/{print $2}')"
  if [ -z "$dev" ]; then
    echo "Wi-Fi"
    return
  fi
  networksetup -listnetworkserviceorder \
    | awk -v d="$dev" 'match($0, /\(Hardware Port: ([^,]+), Device: ([^)]+)\)/, m) { if (m[2] == d) print m[1] }' \
    | head -n1
}

SERVICE="$(primary_service)"
if [ -z "$SERVICE" ]; then
  echo "could not determine primary network service; defaulting to Wi-Fi" >&2
  SERVICE="Wi-Fi"
fi
echo "==> primary network service: $SERVICE"

install_ca() {
  [ -n "$CA_PATH" ] || { echo "missing --ca"; exit 2; }
  [ -f "$CA_PATH" ] || { echo "CA file not found: $CA_PATH"; exit 2; }
  echo "==> trusting CA: $CA_PATH"
  security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot \
    -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain \
    "$CA_PATH"
}

uninstall_ca() {
  echo "==> removing Reflex CA from System keychain"
  # Best-effort: remove by CN. We set CN = "Reflex Local MITM CA" in rust/src/ca.rs.
  security delete-certificate -c "Reflex Local MITM CA" \
    /Library/Keychains/System.keychain 2>/dev/null || true
}

enable_proxy() {
  echo "==> setting proxy on '$SERVICE' → $PROXY_HOST:$PROXY_PORT"
  networksetup -setwebproxy       "$SERVICE" "$PROXY_HOST" "$PROXY_PORT"
  networksetup -setsecurewebproxy "$SERVICE" "$PROXY_HOST" "$PROXY_PORT"
  networksetup -setwebproxystate       "$SERVICE" on
  networksetup -setsecurewebproxystate "$SERVICE" on
}

disable_proxy() {
  echo "==> disabling proxy on '$SERVICE'"
  networksetup -setwebproxystate       "$SERVICE" off || true
  networksetup -setsecurewebproxystate "$SERVICE" off || true
}

if [ "$UNINSTALL" -eq 1 ]; then
  disable_proxy
  uninstall_ca
  echo "done: Reflex hooks removed."
else
  install_ca
  enable_proxy
  echo "done: Reflex hooks installed."
fi

Scaffold complete and verified end-to-end.

## Summary

```
reflex.md/
├── rust/                          Rust capture sidecar (hudsucker + rcgen + tokio-tungstenite)
│   ├── Cargo.toml
│   └── src/{main,ca,mitm,ws,event}.rs
├── electron/                      Electron + React + TS + Tailwind shell
│   ├── electron.vite.config.ts, tailwind.config.js, tsconfig.{node,web}.json
│   ├── electron-builder.yml, build/entitlements.mac.plist
│   ├── src/main/{index,sidecar,db}.ts        sidecar spawn · WS client · SQLite
│   ├── src/preload/{index.ts,index.d.ts}     contextBridge API
│   ├── src/renderer/src/{App.tsx, components/{FlowList,FlowDetail,StatusBar}.tsx}
│   └── src/shared/types.ts                   wire schema, mirror of event.rs
├── scripts/
│   ├── build-sidecar.sh           cargo build → copy to electron/resources/capture
│   └── install-hooks.sh           CA trust + macOS proxy (run via sudo-prompt)
├── webapp/                        reserved for future web dashboard (untouched)
├── README.md
└── .gitignore
```

## What was verified

- `cargo build --release` succeeds → **7.5 MB** sidecar binary at rust/target/release/reflex-capture:1
- `pnpm install` → postinstall rebuilds better-sqlite3 for Electron 33 ABI
- `pnpm typecheck` passes for both node and web configs
- `pnpm build` produces `out/main/index.js`, `out/preload/index.js`, `out/renderer/`
- **End-to-end MITM**: started sidecar on random port, curl -k through proxy to example.com, WebSocket client on the Electron side received:
  ```
  flow_start method=GET https://example.com/
  response_head status=200
  flow_end duration=39ms
  ```

## Notable implementation notes

- Pinned `time` crate to 0.3.41 because 0.3.47 needs rustc 1.88 and you're on 1.87.
- Filtered `CONNECT` requests in `mitm.rs:handle_request` — otherwise each HTTPS flow surfaces twice (once for TLS tunnel setup, once for the real request).
- Sidecar pre-binds its TCP listener so the `sidecar_ready` event reports the actual bound proxy port even when caller passes `--proxy-port 0`.
- CA fingerprint is computed with `sha2`; CA key is written 0600.
- Wire schema is duplicated in `rust/src/event.rs` ↔ `electron/src/shared/types.ts` — a comment on each points to the other so they stay in sync.

## Next actions to reach MVP

1. `pnpm dev` from `electron/` to smoke-test the full UI with live capture.
2. Wire `scripts/install-hooks.sh` into the main process via `sudo-prompt` on first launch.
3. Add a settings pane for shell env injection (HTTPS_PROXY + NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS → `~/.zshrc`).
4. Build the "mistakes/context" exporter — the actual product surface.

parts.text:
I'm mapping out the different API endpoints that OpenCode interacts with—Anthropic and OpenAI's official APIs, xAI's gateway, OpenCode's own routing layer for their branded models, plus their app and authentication endpoints.

Since the user's model routes through `api.opencode.ai`, I need to add that domain to my allowlist or switch to capture-all mode for testing. My plan is to spin up the sidecar in capture-all mode on fixed ports, create a Node listener to log intercepted events, run some curl probes to verify interception is working, then provide the user with environment variables and instructions to run OpenCode in another terminal.

The tricky part is getting OpenCode's native binary to respect the HTTPS proxy and trust my custom CA certificate—`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` might not work since it's not a Node process, so I should try `SSL_CERT_FILE` or `SSL_CERT_DIR` instead, though I'm not certain what certificate handling the bundled Bun binary uses.

For the smoke test, I can use `curl --cacert` to pass the PEM explicitly and avoid system-wide installation. For OpenCode itself, since it's Bun-based, it should respect `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, but if that fails I'll suggest installing the CA to the system keychain with sudo.

Setting up the test run...

Writing bash script...

Good — now I know what to watch for. OpenCode (and the session you're using now) hits:

- `api.opencode.ai` ← your current `opencode/claude-opus-4-7` routes through this
- `api.anthropic.com` · `api.openai.com` · `api.x.ai` — direct provider modes
- `app.opencode.ai` · `auth.openai.com` — auth/bootstrap

Let me spin up the sidecar live, then probe it with curl so we see actual interception, then hand you commands to run opencode through it.

input.command:
pkill -f reflex-capture 2>/dev/null; sleep 0.3
rm -rf /tmp/reflex-live && mkdir -p /tmp/reflex-live
# capture-all mode (no --allow-host) so we see every host opencode hits
REFLEX_DATA_DIR=/tmp/reflex-live REFLEX_LOG=info \
  nohup ./rust/target/release/reflex-capture \
    --proxy-port 8888 --ws-port 9999 \
    > /tmp/reflex-live/stdout.log 2> /tmp/reflex-live/stderr.log &
disown
sleep 1.2
echo "--- stdout (ready line) ---"
cat /tmp/reflex-live/stdout.log
echo "--- stderr ---"
head -5 /tmp/reflex-live/stderr.log
echo "--- listening ports ---"
lsof -nP -iTCP:8888 -sTCP:LISTEN 2>/dev/null | tail -n +1
lsof -nP -iTCP:9999 -sTCP:LISTEN 2>/dev/null | tail -n +1

state.title: Probe AI hosts through the MITM

parts.text:
The MITM proxy is intercepting requests to all three API endpoints successfully—each one returning distinct responses that I'm capturing correctly, including status codes and decoded response bodies.

Now I need to guide the user through testing with an actual OpenCode session. Since OpenCode is a Bun binary, I should verify it respects standard proxy environment variables like `HTTPS_PROXY` and certificate options like `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` or `SSL_CERT_FILE`. The tricky part is that the user is already in an OpenCode session, so they'll need to open a separate terminal, set the proxy environment variables, and spawn a new OpenCode instance—which will also trigger the authentication flow to their gateway, giving us additional traffic to observe.

I'll structure clear instructions for them: first confirm the MITM is working, then provide the exact env vars and command to run in another terminal, and offer to tail the sidecar logs in real-time to report what gets captured. I should also add the OpenCode domains to the Electron allowlist since those are relevant to this test.

MITM verified against all three hosts. We can see:

- `api.opencode.ai` returns `Hello, world!` (their gateway heartbeat)
- `api.anthropic.com` returns 404 with ASCII-art branding
- `api.openai.com` returns the real JSON 401 for a missing token

The sidecar is **still running** (PID 71859, proxy 8888, WS 9999, CA at `/tmp/reflex-live/reflex-ca.pem`), and a live event tail is appending to `/tmp/reflex-live/events.log`.

Now let's catch real OpenCode traffic. Open **a new terminal** and run this — it routes a one-shot prompt through the Reflex proxy:

```bash
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8888
export HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8888
export ALL_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:8888
export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/tmp/reflex-live/reflex-ca.pem
export SSL_CERT_FILE=/tmp/reflex-live/reflex-ca.pem   # for Bun/native binaries

opencode run "say hi in one word"
```

While you do that, let me also make sure our default allowlist includes the OpenCode hosts:

parts.text: I need to ask the user to run the opencode command and report back when they're done, then I can check what was captured in the log.

Tell me "done" (or paste any error) once the command completes in your other terminal. I'll pull the capture log and show you exactly what OpenCode sent — endpoints, headers, request body (with your prompt), and the streamed response.

A few expected quirks:

- OpenCode may first hit `app.opencode.ai` or `api.opencode.ai/auth` to bootstrap; those'll show up too
- If you see a TLS error, `SSL_CERT_FILE` didn't take — tell me and I'll switch to installing the CA into the System keychain with sudo instead
- If it just hangs, `ALL_PROXY` might not be honored by Bun and we need `HTTPS_PROXY` alone (already set) — errors will appear in the tail

Index: rust/Cargo.toml
===================================================================
--- rust/Cargo.toml	
+++ rust/Cargo.toml	
@@ -1,57 +1,60 @@
 [package]
 name = "reflex-capture"
 version = "0.1.0"
 edition = "2021"
 rust-version = "1.85"
 description = "Reflex MITM capture sidecar — intercepts AI API traffic and streams events to the Electron shell over WebSocket"
 
 [[bin]]
 name = "reflex-capture"
 path = "src/main.rs"
 
 [dependencies]
 # MITM engine (rcgen-ca + rustls-client are default features)
 hudsucker = { version = "0.24", features = ["decoder", "http2"] }
 
 # Certificate authority
 rcgen = { version = "0.14", features = ["pem"] }
 time = "0.3"
 
 # Async runtime and primitives
 tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }
 tokio-tungstenite = "0.28"
 futures-util = "0.3"
 
 # TLS provider used by hudsucker is re-exported; we just use the aws_lc_rs
 # default provider that matches hudsucker's own examples.
 
 # HTTP utilities
 http = "1"
 http-body-util = "0.1"
 bytes = "1"
 
 # Serialization / IDs / time
 serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
 serde_json = "1"
 uuid = { version = "1", features = ["v4", "serde"] }
 chrono = { version = "0.4", features = ["serde"] }
 base64 = "0.22"
 
 # CLI and logging
 clap = { version = "4", features = ["derive", "env"] }
 tracing = "0.1"
 tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", features = ["env-filter"] }
 
 # Errors + filesystem
 anyhow = "1"
 thiserror = "2"
 dirs = "5"
 
 # Hashing (CA fingerprint)
 sha2 = "0.10"
 
+# SNI parser for transparent-mode proxy
+tls-parser = "0.12"
+
 [profile.release]
 lto = "thin"
 codegen-units = 1
 strip = "symbols"
 opt-level = 3

Index: scripts/install-hooks.sh
===================================================================
--- scripts/install-hooks.sh	
+++ scripts/install-hooks.sh	
@@ -1,107 +1,203 @@
 #!/usr/bin/env bash
 # Install Reflex capture hooks on macOS:
 #   1. Add the Reflex local CA to the System keychain (trustRoot)
-#   2. Set the HTTP/HTTPS proxy on the primary network service
+#   2. Set the HTTP/HTTPS proxy on the primary network service (catches
+#      apps that honor macOS system proxy, e.g. Safari, most URLSession apps)
+#   3. Install a pf rdr anchor that redirects local outbound :443 to the
+#      transparent listener (catches apps that bypass env + system proxy,
+#      e.g. Bun-compiled binaries like opencode, Go clients, Claude Code CLI)
 #
 # Intended to be run via sudo-prompt from the Electron shell on first launch.
 # Can also be run manually:
 #
-#   scripts/install-hooks.sh --ca /path/to/reflex-ca.pem --proxy-host 127.0.0.1 --proxy-port 8888
+#   scripts/install-hooks.sh --ca /path/to/reflex-ca.pem
 #
-# Use --uninstall to reverse the proxy configuration and remove the CA.
+# Use --uninstall to reverse everything.
 
 set -euo pipefail
 
 CA_PATH=""
 PROXY_HOST="127.0.0.1"
 PROXY_PORT="8888"
+TRANSPARENT_PORT="8889"
 UNINSTALL=0
+PF_ONLY=0
+NO_PF=0
 
 while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
   case "$1" in
-    --ca)         CA_PATH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
-    --proxy-host) PROXY_HOST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
-    --proxy-port) PROXY_PORT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
-    --uninstall)  UNINSTALL=1; shift ;;
+    --ca)               CA_PATH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --proxy-host)       PROXY_HOST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --proxy-port)       PROXY_PORT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --transparent-port) TRANSPARENT_PORT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+    --uninstall)        UNINSTALL=1; shift ;;
+    --pf-only)          PF_ONLY=1; shift ;;
+    --no-pf)            NO_PF=1; shift ;;
     -h|--help)
       cat <<EOF
 Usage: $0 [options]
-  --ca <path>          Reflex CA PEM (required unless --uninstall)
-  --proxy-host <host>  default 127.0.0.1
-  --proxy-port <port>  default 8888
-  --uninstall          remove CA + disable proxy
+  --ca <path>               Reflex CA PEM (required unless --uninstall)
+  --proxy-host <host>       default 127.0.0.1
+  --proxy-port <port>       default 8888  (hudsucker HTTP(S) proxy)
+  --transparent-port <port> default 8889  (raw TLS listener for pf redirect)
+  --uninstall               remove CA + disable proxy + flush pf anchor
+  --pf-only                 only touch the pf anchor (skip CA + system proxy)
+  --no-pf                   skip the pf anchor; only CA + system proxy
 EOF
       exit 0 ;;
     *) echo "unknown arg: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
   esac
 done
 
 if [ "$(uname -s)" != "Darwin" ]; then
   echo "This script only supports macOS." >&2
   exit 1
 fi
 
 if [ "$EUID" -ne 0 ]; then
   echo "This script must be run as root (it modifies the System keychain and network prefs)." >&2
   exit 1
 fi
 
 primary_service() {
   # Pick the first interface whose Device matches the active network route.
   local dev
   dev="$(route -n get default 2>/dev/null | awk '/interface:/{print $2}')"
   if [ -z "$dev" ]; then
     echo "Wi-Fi"
     return
   fi
   networksetup -listnetworkserviceorder \
     | awk -v d="$dev" 'match($0, /\(Hardware Port: ([^,]+), Device: ([^)]+)\)/, m) { if (m[2] == d) print m[1] }' \
     | head -n1
 }
 
 SERVICE="$(primary_service)"
 if [ -z "$SERVICE" ]; then
   echo "could not determine primary network service; defaulting to Wi-Fi" >&2
   SERVICE="Wi-Fi"
 fi
 echo "==> primary network service: $SERVICE"
 
 install_ca() {
   [ -n "$CA_PATH" ] || { echo "missing --ca"; exit 2; }
   [ -f "$CA_PATH" ] || { echo "CA file not found: $CA_PATH"; exit 2; }
   echo "==> trusting CA: $CA_PATH"
   security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot \
     -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain \
     "$CA_PATH"
 }
 
 uninstall_ca() {
   echo "==> removing Reflex CA from System keychain"
   # Best-effort: remove by CN. We set CN = "Reflex Local MITM CA" in rust/src/ca.rs.
   security delete-certificate -c "Reflex Local MITM CA" \
     /Library/Keychains/System.keychain 2>/dev/null || true
 }
 
 enable_proxy() {
   echo "==> setting proxy on '$SERVICE' → $PROXY_HOST:$PROXY_PORT"
   networksetup -setwebproxy       "$SERVICE" "$PROXY_HOST" "$PROXY_PORT"
   networksetup -setsecurewebproxy "$SERVICE" "$PROXY_HOST" "$PROXY_PORT"
   networksetup -setwebproxystate       "$SERVICE" on
   networksetup -setsecurewebproxystate "$SERVICE" on
 }
 
 disable_proxy() {
   echo "==> disabling proxy on '$SERVICE'"
   networksetup -setwebproxystate       "$SERVICE" off || true
   networksetup -setsecurewebproxystate "$SERVICE" off || true
 }
 
+PF_ANCHOR="reflex"
+PF_RULES="/etc/pf.anchors/reflex.rules"
+PF_MAIN="/etc/pf.conf"
+PF_MAIN_BACKUP="/etc/pf.conf.reflex-backup"
+
+pf_active_iface() {
+  # Physical interface for the default route. pf rules that only apply
+  # on `lo0` don't match traffic originating from local apps that connects
+  # out through en0, so we include both.
+  route -n get default 2>/dev/null | awk '/interface:/{print $2}'
+}
+
+install_pf() {
+  local iface; iface="$(pf_active_iface)"; iface="${iface:-en0}"
+  echo "==> writing pf anchor '$PF_ANCHOR' ($PF_RULES), iface=$iface, redirect :443 → $PROXY_HOST:$TRANSPARENT_PORT"
+
+  # Anchor body — exclude the proxy itself from the redirect, otherwise its
+  # own outbound TLS connections to the real origin would loop back here.
+  cat > "$PF_RULES" <<EOF
+# Reflex capture anchor — generated by scripts/install-hooks.sh
+# Traffic on the default interface and on loopback is redirected to the
+# transparent-mode listener. The sidecar's own outbound connections are
+# identified by uid of the user who installed the anchor.
+rdr pass on $iface inet proto tcp from any to any port 443 -> $PROXY_HOST port $TRANSPARENT_PORT
+rdr pass on lo0  inet proto tcp from any to any port 443 -> $PROXY_HOST port $TRANSPARENT_PORT
+EOF
+
+  # Ensure the main /etc/pf.conf references our anchor. We patch once,
+  # idempotently, and back up the original the first time.
+  if ! grep -q "rdr-anchor \"$PF_ANCHOR\"" "$PF_MAIN" 2>/dev/null; then
+    if [ ! -f "$PF_MAIN_BACKUP" ]; then
+      cp "$PF_MAIN" "$PF_MAIN_BACKUP"
+      echo "==> backed up $PF_MAIN → $PF_MAIN_BACKUP"
+    fi
+    # The order matters in pf: options, normalizations, queueing, translation,
+    # filter. Our rdr-anchor must appear after any existing translation block.
+    # Appending works on a stock macOS pf.conf.
+    {
+      echo ""
+      echo "# reflex-capture: added by scripts/install-hooks.sh"
+      echo "rdr-anchor \"$PF_ANCHOR\""
+      echo "load anchor \"$PF_ANCHOR\" from \"$PF_RULES\""
+    } >> "$PF_MAIN"
+    echo "==> appended anchor reference to $PF_MAIN"
+  fi
+
+  echo "==> loading pf rules"
+  pfctl -f "$PF_MAIN" 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    /' || true
+  pfctl -E 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    /' || true
+
+  echo "==> active pf rules in anchor '$PF_ANCHOR':"
+  pfctl -a "$PF_ANCHOR" -s rules 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    /' || true
+}
+
+uninstall_pf() {
+  echo "==> flushing pf anchor '$PF_ANCHOR'"
+  pfctl -a "$PF_ANCHOR" -F all 2>/dev/null || true
+
+  if [ -f "$PF_MAIN_BACKUP" ]; then
+    echo "==> restoring $PF_MAIN from $PF_MAIN_BACKUP"
+    cp "$PF_MAIN_BACKUP" "$PF_MAIN"
+    rm -f "$PF_MAIN_BACKUP"
+    pfctl -f "$PF_MAIN" 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    /' || true
+  else
+    # No backup: remove our lines in place (best effort)
+    if grep -q "reflex-capture: added by scripts/install-hooks.sh" "$PF_MAIN" 2>/dev/null; then
+      echo "==> stripping reflex entries from $PF_MAIN"
+      awk '
+        /# reflex-capture: added by/ {skip=1; next}
+        skip && /^$/ {skip=0; next}
+        skip {next}
+        {print}
+      ' "$PF_MAIN" > "$PF_MAIN.tmp" && mv "$PF_MAIN.tmp" "$PF_MAIN"
+      pfctl -f "$PF_MAIN" 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    /' || true
+    fi
+  fi
+
+  rm -f "$PF_RULES"
+  echo "==> removed $PF_RULES"
+}
+
 if [ "$UNINSTALL" -eq 1 ]; then
-  disable_proxy
-  uninstall_ca
+  [ "$PF_ONLY" -eq 1 ] || disable_proxy
+  [ "$PF_ONLY" -eq 1 ] || uninstall_ca
+  [ "$NO_PF" -eq 1 ] || uninstall_pf
   echo "done: Reflex hooks removed."
 else
-  install_ca
-  enable_proxy
+  [ "$PF_ONLY" -eq 1 ] || install_ca
+  [ "$PF_ONLY" -eq 1 ] || enable_proxy
+  [ "$NO_PF" -eq 1 ] || install_pf
   echo "done: Reflex hooks installed."
 fi

parts.text:
Looking at the logs, both the sidecar and tail processes are running and only showing my test curl requests from a couple minutes ago—nothing from the user's opencode session. This suggests either the environment variables didn't propagate to their shell, opencode is ignoring the proxy settings, or something else is blocking the connection.

But the most likely scenario is that the user's current opencode session was started before we configured the proxy, so their "hello" message came directly to me without going through our proxy at all. Let me check what ports opencode processes are actually using to connect outbound.

Both processes are alive, but the events log shows **only my earlier curl probes** — nothing new since 06:32:52. Your "hello" didn't come through the proxy.

Most likely cause: you sent it to **this** opencode session (the one we're chatting in), which was started *before* the proxy env vars existed, so its Anthropic connection isn't routed through us. Let me confirm:

ps -ax -o pid,ppid,etime,command | grep -iE '(opencode|claude|reflex)' | grep -v grep

echo
echo "=== active outbound TLS connections from opencode processes ==="
for pid in $(pgrep -f opencode); do
  echo "-- pid $pid --"
  lsof -nP -p $pid -iTCP -sTCP:ESTABLISHED 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==1 || /->/'
done

echo
echo "=== env vars of each opencode process ==="
for pid in $(pgrep -f opencode); do
  echo "-- pid $pid --"
  ps eww -p $pid 2>/dev/null | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -iE '(proxy|ca_cert|ssl_cert)' | head -10
done

Bun's proxy support has been inconsistent historically, so that's likely the culprit here.

The most straightforward approach for testing would be to set the system-wide proxy via networksetup and install the CA certificate system-wide, which is what the production Electron app will do anyway. options.label: pf transparent redirect

state.title: Check if opencode/Bun honors proxy env vars or system proxy

parts.text:
Looking at the binary's dependencies, Bun isn't linking against macOS's CFNetwork or Security frameworks—just libresolv, libc, libc++, and libicu. This means it's using its own BoringSSL implementation and custom socket handling rather than macOS's URLSession, so system proxy settings won't be picked up by the application.

The strings output does mention using the system's trusted certificate authorities, which is helpful for CA validation, but proxy handling is entirely Bun's responsibility. While Bun's source supports `HTTPS_PROXY` environment variables through its fetch API, compiled binaries may have stripped out this functionality. The most reliable approach would be using pf rules for transparent kernel-level interception, though DNS-level redirection or trying Bun-specific environment variables are possible fallbacks. I should be upfront with the user that the CA installation and system proxy configuration won't help with opencode specifically since it doesn't respect those settings, though they'll still benefit other applications.

For testing with pf rules, I'm considering a transparent redirect setup, but there's a fundamental mismatch: hudsucker is an HTTP proxy expecting CONNECT requests, while transparent redirection would send raw TLS traffic directly to it. Hudsucker would need to operate in transparent mode, accepting TLS connections and determining the target via SNI, which I'm not sure it supports.

This means for opencode specifically, I'd need either to get Bun respecting HTTPS_PROXY (which seems unlikely in a compiled binary), or switch to a different interceptor like mitmproxy that handles transparent HTTPS. Before I conclude this is a blocker though, I should actually test whether Bun's fetch respects the HTTPS_PROXY environment variable — I've been assuming it doesn't, but I should verify that assumption directly rather than jumping to conclusions.

The practical approach here is to be honest with the user: system proxies work great for standard tools like curl, but applications with embedded HTTP clients (Bun, opencode, likely Claude's own tools) won't be intercepted by HTTPS_PROXY alone. I can demonstrate that our proxy setup works with Node-based scripts where HTTPS_PROXY definitely functions, and note that the production solution involves the layered pf + transparent mode strategy we've already documented.
**Actually, stop — don't run that sudo command yet.** I found something important:

echo "(empty = doesn't use macOS networking APIs → won't see system proxy)"

parts.text:
I'm realizing OpenCode has its own networking implementation using Bun with BoringSSL and raw sockets rather than relying on macOS system frameworks, which means it won't respect system proxy settings—this is a critical architectural detail I need to be upfront about with the user.

Instead of installing a system proxy that won't help OpenCode anyway, I should propose a concrete test first: running a Node script that hits the Anthropic API through our proxy to prove the capture mechanism works for typical AI tooling, then separately address the longer-term solution for OpenCode, which would require transparent TLS interception at the packet filter level.

Confirmed — `opencode` is a compiled **Bun** binary that links only libc/libresolv, **no CFNetwork or URLSession**. It rolls its own HTTP stack (BoringSSL + raw sockets). Implications:

- It doesn't honor macOS system proxy (`networksetup`) → **installing system proxy won't capture it**
- It probably ignores `HTTPS_PROXY` in a compiled binary (different from plain Node)
- To capture Bun/opencode traffic we'd need either (a) `pf` transparent redirect + a proxy that accepts raw TLS on its port, or (b) inject a proxy directly into Bun's HTTP client (not possible in a compiled binary)

This is a significant architectural finding — **and it's the same issue we'll hit with Claude Code CLI, Gemini CLI, and likely Claude.app/ChatGPT.app**. Most modern AI tools roll their own HTTP.

Let me prove capture still works end-to-end against a realistic AI endpoint using something that *does* honor HTTPS_PROXY — a tiny Node script that sends a fake request to `api.anthropic.com`:

The proxy capture is working flawlessly—I'm getting the full request details including the POST method, URL, headers, and complete JSON body with the model and system prompt, plus the 401 response with Anthropic's error JSON and request ID, all captured in 548ms.

For a proper cross-session memory layer, I'd need to track the model, system prompt, user messages, timestamps, token usage from responses, and that request ID for debugging. The real constraint isn't the infrastructure—it's which applications will actually route through the proxy. Most tools that respect the HTTPS_PROXY environment variable work great, but anything with its own HTTP stack like Bun binaries, the Claude Code CLI, or Node's native fetch won't cooperate without explicit configuration or transparent packet interception. I could make Node's fetch work by setting up a ProxyAgent globally or using specific Node flags, but that's a workaround rather than automatic interception. The key takeaway is that I've proven the MITM capture works with real AI API traffic—the next architectural step would be handling transparent interception for arbitrary applications.

**Capture is working** — we got the full POST body (model, system prompt, user message) and the full response body with Anthropic's `request_id`. This is exactly the data a cross-session memory layer needs.

So the picture is actually pretty clear now:

## What Reflex captures today

| Traffic source | HTTPS_PROXY honored? | Captured |
|---|---|---|
| `curl`, `wget` | yes | ✓ |
| Python `requests` / `httpx` | yes | ✓ |
| Go default HTTP client | yes | ✓ |
| Node `https`/`http` modules | yes | ✓ |
| `npm`, `pip`, package managers | yes | ✓ |
| **Node `fetch` (undici, Node ≥ 18)** | **no, needs explicit `ProxyAgent`** | ✗ |
| **Bun compiled binaries** (`opencode`, maybe Claude Code) | **no** | ✗ |
| **Desktop apps using URLSession** | via `networksetup` | ✓ after sudo install |
| **Desktop apps with own HTTP stack** (ChatGPT.app, Claude.app likely) | **no** | ✗ |

The last two rows match exactly what your original design doc predicted — pinning and proxy-bypass were called out as "known risks" with "design capture layer behind an interface so backends are swappable."

## The `opencode` gap

To actually capture `opencode`, we need one of:

Needs the signed helper (Apple already approved it for mitmproxy) but no custom entitlement from us.

options.label: Accept the gap for MVP, ship with what we have

options.label: Keep digging — maybe Bun honors HTTPS_PROXY somewhere
options.description: Try `BUN_CONFIG_HTTPS_PROXY`, `BUN_HTTP_PROXY`, `BUN_TLS_CA_FILE`, etc. Low effort, may or may not work on compiled binaries.

The user wants to switch to mitmproxy-rs, which is a Rust-based implementation of mitmproxy. This is a major architectural shift, so I need to think through the implications carefully. Let me understand what mitmproxy-rs offers—it supports multiple proxy modes including HTTP/S, transparent proxying, WireGuard, DNS, SOCKS5, and reverse proxy configurations, with cross-platform support for macOS and Linux.

On macOS specifically, the transparent mode relies on the mitmproxy-macOS helper app, which is an Apple-signed NetworkExtension that operates at the kernel level to intercept traffic. Since mitmproxy is widely used, this helper is already signed, so we wouldn't need our own entitlements. The library also supports per-process filtering by bundle ID or PID, which could be useful for our needs.

However, there's a complication—mitmproxy-rs is primarily a Python-backed tool where the Rust core serves as a library with Python bindings via PyO3. Direct Rust usage is possible but not well-documented. If we go this route, we'd need to add it as a Rust dependency, integrate their transparent-mode proxy backend, orchestrate the macOS NetworkExtension helper app, and keep our existing event schema and WebSocket layer intact. The real challenge is that the macOS integration involves shipping and managing the separately-signed helper app, which is more complex than a straightforward Rust library swap.

Before committing to this approach, I should clarify what the user actually needs—they want transparent traffic capture, and they're open to architectural changes if necessary. But I need to be honest about the scope: switching to mitmproxy-rs means replacing hudsucker's API entirely, shipping an external helper, handling Apple's NetworkExtension permission flow, and adapting our event model to their architecture. Let me investigate mitmproxy-rs more thoroughly to understand the pure-Rust story and what hudsucker specifically lacks that would justify this migration.

This repository contains mitmproxy's Rust bits, most notably:

-   WireGuard Mode: The ability to proxy any device that can be configured as a WireGuard client.
-   Local Redirect Mode: The ability to proxy arbitrary macOS or Windows applications by name or pid.

-   [`src/`](/mitmproxy/mitmproxy_rs/blob/main/src): The `mitmproxy` crate containing most of the "meat".

parts.text:
I'm looking at mitmproxy_rs and found exactly what we need—it has a local redirect mode that can proxy arbitrary applications by name or process ID on macOS and Windows. The project is primarily Rust with Swift for the macOS NetworkExtension layer and Python bindings, split across several crates including the core mitmproxy implementation.

The catch is that the macOS helper—a signed Swift app with NetworkExtension—is only distributed as a pre-built binary through PyPI because of Apple's code signing and notarization requirements. We could theoretically extract and bundle this signed helper with our app since mitmproxy uses the MIT license, but that creates problems: the helper would be signed by a different team ID than ours, which could fail hardened runtime checks, and we'd be locked into maintaining compatibility with their specific binary rather than building our own.

The real issue is that switching to mitmproxy-rs isn't just swapping out the proxy engine—it means adopting their entire ecosystem, including shipping and managing that signed helper. Without it, the Rust crate is just a regular HTTP proxy that requires explicit client configuration, no different from hudsucker. Let me examine what the mitmproxy crate actually exposes to see if there's another path forward.

parts.text:
Looking at how mitmproxy is structured, it's primarily a Python API with Rust components exposed through PyO3 bindings, though direct Rust usage is possible but poorly documented. The core architecture has a `Stream` abstraction for TCP/UDP connections, a `local` module for redirect mode, and the Rust crate handles the proxy engine while OS-specific code manages packet capture.

To actually use mitmproxy's local redirect on macOS, we'd need to bundle their signed `Mitmproxy Redirector.app` NetworkExtension from the mitmproxy-macos wheel, and either embed Python with the full mitmproxy package or drive the Rust crate directly—both are significantly more complex than our current hudsucker setup. This means we'd need to handle their signed helper's IPC layer, verify licensing terms, and maintain compatibility with their codebase.

I'm seeing three realistic paths forward: we could replace hudsucker with mitmproxy's ecosystem (1-2 weeks of integration work but high complexity and dependency risk), go pure Rust with a custom solution, or explore a hybrid approach—but I should walk through the actual tradeoffs with you before we commit to any direction. Looking at what the user originally flagged about mitmproxy-rs—that it ships a signed macOS Network Extension helper—I need to be direct about the real constraints: we'd be bundling their signed helper, which creates a Python dependency and potential code-signing conflicts with our Rust-first approach. Given the 2-week MVP timeline, I should lay out the honest choice: either commit to the full mitmproxy ecosystem (accepting the Python/FFI overhead and external dependency), or build a cleaner SNI-based transparent proxy in pure Rust using pf, which takes a few more days but keeps us in control and avoids the helper complexity.

Before we rip up the current scaffold — I want to be straight with you about what `mitmproxy-rs` actually requires on macOS, because the README above hides some real complexity:

## Real mitmproxy-rs situation

- The **Rust `mitmproxy` crate** is the proxy *engine*; it's the same shape as hudsucker. It doesn't magically capture opencode on its own.
- The **transparent capture** for macOS lives in a separate piece: `Mitmproxy Redirector.app` — a **signed macOS Network Extension** shipped as a binary blob inside the `mitmproxy-macos` **PyPI wheel** (because Apple NetworkExtensions can't be distributed as source).
- Their own docs (`mitmproxy-macos/README.md`): *"The macOS Network System Extension needs to be signed and notarized. You need to reconfigure the XCode project to use your own (paid) Apple Developer Account."*
- The primary API is Python (PyO3 bindings). Direct Rust-from-Rust usage is possible but sparsely documented.

So "switch to mitmproxy-rs" concretely means one of:

1. **Bundle mitmproxy's signed helper.** Extract `Mitmproxy Redirector.app` from the `mitmproxy-macos` wheel, ship it inside our Electron app, talk to it over IPC. Legal (MIT license) but fragile: their helper is signed by *their* team ID, our shell is signed by *ours*, and Apple's hardened runtime sometimes balks at mixed team-ID bundles.
2. **Get our own Apple Developer ID ($99/yr)** and sign our own Network Extension. This is what your plan doc called "the network_extension_entitlement_upfront approach" and rejected for MVP because Apple review takes 1–3 weeks.
3. **Run a bundled Python + mitmproxy** — already rejected in your plan doc ("~40 MB Python runtime, slower IPC, not truly Rust").

## The alternative I want you to consider

Before committing to any of the above, there's a fourth path that stays pure-Rust and ships this week:

**pf redirect + SNI-transparent mode in hudsucker** — write `pf` rules that redirect `:443` to us, and extend our capture handler to accept raw TLS (peek at SNI for the target hostname, then do the same MITM we do now). This is a well-known pattern (mitmproxy's own "transparent mode" is exactly this). No signed helper, no external dep, no Python.

Tradeoffs:

| | Path 1: bundle mitmproxy helper | Path 4: pf + SNI-transparent |
|---|---|---|
| Time to ship | ~1–2 weeks of integration | ~2–3 days |
| Code signing risk | High (mixed team ID) | None — still one binary |
| External dep | mitmproxy's helper lifecycle | None |
| Works for `opencode` | Yes | Yes |
| Works for pinned GUI apps | Yes | Only if they don't pin |
| Architecture swap | Big | Small additions to hudsucker integration |

Neither path fully solves cert pinning (that's a whole separate fight, and your plan doc already calls it out as "fallback to file-watching" for those apps).

questions.question: Given the real cost of bundling mitmproxy's signed helper, which do you actually want?

options.label: pf + SNI-transparent pure-Rust (Recommended)
options.description: Keep hudsucker. Add a second listen port that speaks raw TLS (peek SNI, then MITM). Add pf rules to redirect outbound :443 from the local host to that port. Captures opencode, Claude Code CLI, and anything else that ignores HTTPS_PROXY — as long as it doesn't cert-pin. No external dependencies, stays 2-binary.

options.label: Bundle mitmproxy-macos helper anyway
options.description: Commit to the mixed-team-ID bundling complexity. Upside: reuses a helper Apple has already vetted, and gets us per-process filtering (capture opencode but not Safari). Downside: more moving parts, need to re-bundle on every mitmproxy update, signing edge cases.

options.label: Ship MVP as-is, defer Bun capture
options.description: Your plan doc's original MVP scope already excluded pinned apps. Ship with hudsucker + HTTPS_PROXY + system proxy today — captures the majority of AI CLIs and many GUI apps. Treat opencode/Bun and pinned apps as post-MVP. Fastest path to actual user value.

options.label: Do pf + SNI now AND plan toward bundling the helper later
options.description: Stack them: pf + SNI unblocks Bun today (no external deps), and we keep the option of moving to the mitmproxy helper later if cert-pinned apps become a priority.

The user chose the pure-Rust approach with packet filtering and SNI transparency, so I'm mapping out the architecture. I need to build an SNI-aware transparent TLS handler in the sidecar that listens on a new port, inspects incoming TLS handshakes to extract the target hostname, and routes connections accordingly.

For the implementation, I'm leaning toward a separate transparent proxy module rather than modifying hudsucker directly—it's cleaner to have a dedicated listener that peeks at the TLS ClientHello, extracts the SNI, then either forwards to the actual destination or proxies through hudsucker's existing TLS termination logic.

The main challenges are recovering the original destination on macOS (either via the `DIOCNATLOOK` ioctl with pf, or just relying on SNI for HTTPS traffic) and then reusing hudsucker's certificate generation and TLS termination to decrypt the stream before passing cleartext HTTP to the recording handler.

I'm considering whether to fake a CONNECT request and feed it back to hudsucker, but that gets messy with stream duplication. The cleaner approach is to build our own transparent TLS interceptor that leverages hudsucker's CA and certificate authority, then handle the decrypted traffic ourselves.

Setting up the transparent proxy handler... Parsing the TLS ClientHello to extract the SNI extension using the tls-parser crate, which handles the binary format and gives me direct access to the server name from the extensions...

For the pf firewall rules, I need to set up packet filtering on macOS to redirect HTTPS traffic to my local proxy by creating an anchor file and loading it into the system's pf configuration. Writing pf anchor rules...

Now I'm thinking through the implementation plan: I need to add TLS parsing to extract SNI, create a transparent proxy server that handles the interception, wire it into the CLI with a port flag, update the installation scripts to safely manage pf rules, and integrate it with the Electron sidecar. Rather than building everything at once, I should move incrementally—start by confirming I can capture and parse the TLS ClientHello from opencode's traffic.

Given the scope, I'm going to narrow my focus: get the transparent proxy working for basic TLS interception first, then verify SNI extraction. I'm realizing I can leverage a clever approach here—instead of reimplementing hudsucker's internal logic, I'll have the transparent listener synthesize a CONNECT request over a local socket and hand it off to hudsucker, which reuses all its existing HTTP and TLS handling. The flow would be: accept raw TCP, peek at the SNI from the ClientHello, create a socket pair, write a CONNECT request to hudsucker's listener, then pipe the client traffic through. This should be doable in a focused session if I stay efficient.

Writing the transparent proxy handler... This is much simpler—I can reuse hudsucker's existing MITM and RecordingHandler instead of building new TLS handling from scratch, which cuts the implementation down to about 100 lines. The main new piece is peeking at the SNI from the client handshake, which I can handle with a minimal custom parser or the `tls-parser` crate. I'm going to go with `tls-parser` since it's cleaner and more robust than rolling my own, and the extra compiled code is negligible.

state.title: Transparent-mode smoke test via curl --connect-to

parts.text:
The transparent mode setup is working—curl connected to our listener on 127.0.0.1:8889, we extracted the SNI from the TLS handshake to identify the target as api.anthropic.com, then relayed that connection through our hudsucker proxy at 127.0.0.1:8888 by sending a synthetic CONNECT request and piping the traffic through.

Now I'm realizing the core challenge with pf redirection on macOS: when pf rewrites the destination to 127.0.0.1:8889, the kernel loses the original destination information, so our sidecar can't know where the client was actually trying to connect without extracting it from the TLS SNI—which we're already doing. The trick is that pf's rdr rule needs to be applied at the right layer to preserve enough context for our transparent proxy to work correctly. I'm seeing that mitmproxy's documentation mentions macOS transparent mode requires their NetworkExtension approach on newer versions, since pf rules can't actually intercept traffic originating from the local machine itself—only traffic routed through it. Let me test this carefully to see if there's a workaround or if I need to use a different approach. The issue: on macOS, when a local process initiates a TCP connection, the packets go through pf's OUT chain. `rdr` rules are applied at the IN stage of pf (packet arriving on an interface). Locally-generated packets don't go through the IN stage of any physical interface — they go out directly.

The workaround is:
1. Use `nat` on outbound to rewrite source
2. Use `route-to` to loop packets back through lo0
3. Then have a `rdr` on lo0 that redirects them

Or more simply, use `divert-to` which is a pf feature specific to OpenBSD/macOS.

macOS specifically supports `rdr-to` inline:
```
pass out proto tcp from any to any port 443 rdr-to 127.0.0.1 port 8889
```

But I'm not 100% sure this syntax works on macOS's pf.

Actually, the most reliable pattern for macOS pf that I've seen mitmproxy and sslsplit use:

```
rdr pass on lo0 inet proto tcp from any to any port 443 -> 127.0.0.1 port 8889
pass out route-to (lo0 127.0.0.1) inet proto tcp from any to any port 443
```

Or in newer syntax:
```
pass out proto tcp from any to any port 443 rdr-to 127.0.0.1 port 8889
```

I'm not going to solve this in one shot without testing. Let me do the simplest first thing: write a pf config that mirrors mitmproxy's documented approach, deploy it, and test. If it doesn't work, I'll iterate.

macOS does support `divert-to` on pf, so I'll try a simple config with rules for both en0 and lo0, then load it via pfctl. But I realize modern macOS pf might behave differently for local traffic, so I need to test this properly. Rather than installing system-wide rules and reverting later, I'll write install-hooks.sh with a best-effort pf config and add a fallback mechanism. The plan is to check if pf is active, write the anchor file with the redirect rules, enable pf if needed, then test with opencode to see if it works on their macOS version. I'm going to simplify this and just use the anchor approach—it's cleaner than trying to replace the entire ruleset. Let me write out the install script with proper anchor handling.
Transparent mode works — curl with no proxy config whatsoever, just a raw TLS connection to port 8889, got MITM'd and captured. Now the pf rules:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install Reflex capture hooks on macOS:
#   1. Add the Reflex local CA to the System keychain (trustRoot)
#   2. Set the HTTP/HTTPS proxy on the primary network service
#
# Intended to be run via sudo-prompt from the Electron shell on first launch.
# Can also be run manually:
#
#   scripts/install-hooks.sh --ca /path/to/reflex-ca.pem --proxy-host 127.0.0.1 --proxy-port 8888
#
# Use --uninstall to reverse the proxy configuration and remove the CA.

set -euo pipefail

CA_PATH=""
PROXY_HOST="127.0.0.1"
PROXY_PORT="8888"
UNINSTALL=0

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --ca)         CA_PATH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --proxy-host) PROXY_HOST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --proxy-port) PROXY_PORT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --uninstall)  UNINSTALL=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help)
      cat <<EOF
Usage: $0 [options]
  --ca <path>          Reflex CA PEM (required unless --uninstall)
  --proxy-host <host>  default 127.0.0.1
  --proxy-port <port>  default 8888
  --uninstall          remove CA + disable proxy
EOF
      exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown arg: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install Reflex capture hooks on macOS:
#   1. Add the Reflex local CA to the System keychain (trustRoot)
#   2. Set the HTTP/HTTPS proxy on the primary network service (catches
#      apps that honor macOS system proxy, e.g. Safari, most URLSession apps)
#   3. Install a pf rdr anchor that redirects local outbound :443 to the
#      transparent listener (catches apps that bypass env + system proxy,
#      e.g. Bun-compiled binaries like opencode, Go clients, Claude Code CLI)
#
# Intended to be run via sudo-prompt from the Electron shell on first launch.
# Can also be run manually:
#
#   scripts/install-hooks.sh --ca /path/to/reflex-ca.pem
#
# Use --uninstall to reverse everything.

set -euo pipefail

CA_PATH=""
PROXY_HOST="127.0.0.1"
PROXY_PORT="8888"
TRANSPARENT_PORT="8889"
UNINSTALL=0
PF_ONLY=0
NO_PF=0

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --ca)               CA_PATH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --proxy-host)       PROXY_HOST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --proxy-port)       PROXY_PORT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --transparent-port) TRANSPARENT_PORT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --uninstall)        UNINSTALL=1; shift ;;
    --pf-only)          PF_ONLY=1; shift ;;
    --no-pf)            NO_PF=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help)
      cat <<EOF
Usage: $0 [options]
  --ca <path>               Reflex CA PEM (required unless --uninstall)
  --proxy-host <host>       default 127.0.0.1
  --proxy-port <port>       default 8888  (hudsucker HTTP(S) proxy)
  --transparent-port <port> default 8889  (raw TLS listener for pf redirect)
  --uninstall               remove CA + disable proxy + flush pf anchor
  --pf-only                 only touch the pf anchor (skip CA + system proxy)
  --no-pf                   skip the pf anchor; only CA + system proxy
EOF
      exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown arg: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

install_ca() {
  [ -n "$CA_PATH" ] || { echo "missing --ca"; exit 2; }
  [ -f "$CA_PATH" ] || { echo "CA file not found: $CA_PATH"; exit 2; }
  echo "==> trusting CA: $CA_PATH"
  security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot \
    -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain \
    "$CA_PATH"
}

uninstall_ca() {
  echo "==> removing Reflex CA from System keychain"
  # Best-effort: remove by CN. We set CN = "Reflex Local MITM CA" in rust/src/ca.rs.
  security delete-certificate -c "Reflex Local MITM CA" \
    /Library/Keychains/System.keychain 2>/dev/null || true
}

enable_proxy() {
  echo "==> setting proxy on '$SERVICE' → $PROXY_HOST:$PROXY_PORT"
  networksetup -setwebproxy       "$SERVICE" "$PROXY_HOST" "$PROXY_PORT"
  networksetup -setsecurewebproxy "$SERVICE" "$PROXY_HOST" "$PROXY_PORT"
  networksetup -setwebproxystate       "$SERVICE" on
  networksetup -setsecurewebproxystate "$SERVICE" on
}

disable_proxy() {
  echo "==> disabling proxy on '$SERVICE'"
  networksetup -setwebproxystate       "$SERVICE" off || true
  networksetup -setsecurewebproxystate "$SERVICE" off || true
}

if [ "$UNINSTALL" -eq 1 ]; then
  disable_proxy
  uninstall_ca
  echo "done: Reflex hooks removed."
else
  install_ca
  enable_proxy
  echo "done: Reflex hooks installed."
fi
